title: French consular dispatches in cipher to Talleyrand captured on the ship Astrea (the Gibraltar packet)
correspondents: Rozier (former French consul, New York) and others → Talleyrand, Minister of External Relations
place: United States → Paris (captured at sea; sent on by US consul John Gavino, Gibraltar)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Miscellaneous Letters of the Department of State (M179 roll 17): John Adams to Timothy Pickering, Quincy, 1 Apr 1799 (naId 55028996), the cover letter; the location of the ciphered packet itself (originals and the Adams copies by Thomas B. Adams and William Shaw) is not established
folio_note: Adams's cover letter is not digitised in the catalogue; the packet held at least two letters from Rozier (Brumaire and Frimaire an VII) plus others; length unknown
status: NARA item description: Adams submits 'a packet of papers sent by the United States Consul at Gibraltar, but they have not been deciphered'. Adams's letter (Founders Online) says no one in Boston would undertake them and James Lovell 'despairs of being able to make a key'. Pickering to Hamilton 18 Jun 1799: Rozier showed his cipher and Pickering checked some coded passages against Rozier's plain copies. So the Rozier letters were checked in part with the writer's own key; the other letters in the packet and a full decipherment are not recorded. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: French consular reporting to Talleyrand at the height of the Quasi-War, read by the Adams administration only through the writer's own selective key demonstration.

title: Rose O'Neal Greenhow, ciphered letters and fragments from her seized correspondence
correspondents: Rose O'Neal Greenhow ↔ Lt. Col. Thomas Jordan (Beauregard's adjutant) and others
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Seized Correspondence of Rose O'Neal Greenhow (entry A1-986, series naId 873765): Letter Written in Cipher on Mourning Paper (naId 1634036), Letter to 'My Dearest Rachel' with Portions in Cipher (naId 1634051), Copy of a Letter Fragment Partially Written in Cipher (naId 6925618), Apparent Interpretation of Torn or Ciphered Message (naId 1634041); more Greenhow papers 'several of which are in cipher' in RG 107, Records Concerning the Conduct and Loyalty of ... U.S. Citizens During the Civil War (series naId 642808, not digitised)
folio_note: 1634036: one leaf in a symbol cipher (dotted squares, triangles, digit-like signs, dot-separated words; about 25 lines, torn with losses), 4 images; 1634051: 6 images; 6925618 and 1634041: 1 image each. Series 873765 has 205 descriptions, all digitised.
status: Images online (1634036 viewed). The catalogue gives no decipherment for these items; 1634041 is described as an 'apparent interpretation' (a contemporary attempt). Greenhow's cipher was broken in 1861 by Pinkerton's service, reportedly from a plain copy, and a key recovered from her effects in 1864 is at the North Carolina State Archives; the Rosenbach read one of her notes with it. Whether each NARA piece has a full reading in print (OR Series II vol. 2) is not checked. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: The best-known Confederate spy's own ciphertexts, with a surviving key and online images; a full transcription and reading of the NARA pieces would settle what each says.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 NARA catalogue sweep (research/nara_catalog/); one image (1634036) viewed

title: Gen. Joseph E. Johnston → Confederate Secretary of War Seddon, telegram with enciphered phrases
correspondents: Joseph E. Johnston → James A. Seddon
shelfmark: NARA RG 109, War Department Collection of Confederate Records, Telegrams Received by the Confederate Secretary of War (series naId 651917), item naId 3854726
folio_note: 1 leaf + docket, 4 images. Clear text with five cipher words, 31 letters: UNIEK CXNKVNED ... JJTRRK ... ISDX KFYHJEER (read from the image; check).
status: Images online (viewed): clear telegram ('Genl Bragg informs me that a Telegram from Louisville of the 10th says that part of the 9th Corps have been sent to reinforce Grant; will not this enable us to [cipher] for this Genl Bragg & should [cipher] over [cipher]'), cipher words in capitals, no interlinear decipherment on the leaf. Confederate Vigenère with the keys MANCHESTERBLUFF, COMPLETEVICTORY, COMERETRIBUTION in three variants gave no plaintext (quick test, this sweep). Probably printed decoded in the Official Records. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: Johnston's proposal, during the Vicksburg siege, for Bragg to act against Rosecrans; short, but a clean test of which Confederate key Johnston's office used.
